intro: Blackrock Mountain is a massive, active volcano that towers between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge. Borne from the cataclysmic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord, its hollowed depths house ancient dwarven masonry, warring armies, and smoldering horrors.

p: Blackrock Mountain did not exist until the climax of the War of the Three Hammers two and a half centuries ago. Facing annihilation by the united armies of Ironforge and the Wildhammer clan, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan reached into the depths of the earth for a weapon. His reckless spell shattered the dimensional barriers and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The resulting apocalypse tore the Redridge range apart, gouging out the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes while thrusting a colossal volcano into the sky. Thaurissan perished in the blast, and the surviving Dark Iron clan was bound into eternal servitude to the Firelord, carving their capital, Shadowforge City, deep within the mountain's roots.

During the First and Second Wars, the mountain took on a grim new significance. Guided by Cho'gall, the Shadow Council claimed the upper fortress of Blackrock Spire with the quiet acquiescence of Ragnaros's minions. Following the sack of Stormwind, Orgrim Doomhammer purged the council and claimed the spire as the fortress capital of the Horde, viewing the shared name with his own Blackrock clan as a fateful omen. Today, the mountain remains a vicious theater of war: the Dark Iron dwarves and their elemental master hold the fiery depths, while the rogue Blackrock orcs, dragonkin, and their dark masters occupy the spires above.
